next_state_election.name: General Election
next_state_election.source_name: New Mexico Secretary of State — Voting & Elections

glance_notes.source_name: New Mexico Secretary of State — Same Day Voter Registration FAQ
glance_notes.text: Same-Day Registration Available: New Mexico allows eligible residents to register or update their registration and vote on the same day during early voting and on Election Day. Same-day registration is available at County Clerk offices, Election Day polling locations and participating expanded early-voting locations.

glance_notes.source_name: New Mexico Secretary of State — Early Voting in Person
glance_notes.text: Early Voting Begins October 6: For the November 3, 2026 General Election, in-person early voting begins at County Clerk offices on October 6. Expanded early-voting locations may begin operating October 17. Early voting ends October 31.

glance_notes.source_name: New Mexico Secretary of State — Absentee and Early Voting
glance_notes.text: No-Excuse Absentee Voting: Any registered New Mexico voter may request an absentee ballot without providing a reason. Eligible voters may also join New Mexico's permanent absentee list to automatically receive an absentee ballot for statewide elections.

register.label: Register to Vote
register.content: Eligible New Mexico residents may register online through NMVOTE, submit a paper registration form, register through certain government agencies or register in person through their County Clerk. To register, a person must be a U.S. citizen, a New Mexico resident and at least 18 years old by Election Day. Eligible 17-year-olds who will turn 18 by the General Election may participate in the associated Primary Election. New Mexico also provides same-day registration during early voting and on Election Day. A person who is currently incarcerated for a felony conviction is not eligible to vote, but voting eligibility is restored automatically after release from incarceration.
register.glance_value: Online, paper and same-day registration available
register.source_name: New Mexico Secretary of State — Voter Registration Information
register.internal_note: New Mexico's registration system includes online registration, paper applications, agency registration and same-day registration. Current New Mexico law restores voting rights automatically upon release from incarceration for a felony conviction; older descriptions requiring completion of probation or parole are outdated. Online registration generally requires identifying information that can be matched with the Motor Vehicle Division.

check_registration.label: Check Voter Registration
check_registration.content: Use NMVOTE, New Mexico's official Voter Information Portal, to check your voter registration and election information. The portal also provides sample ballots, absentee-ballot applications and status information, voting locations and County Clerk contact information.
check_registration.source_name: New Mexico Secretary of State — NMVOTE Voter Information Portal
check_registration.internal_note: The Secretary of State's current Voting & Elections page directly identifies NMVOTE as the official portal for viewing registration and election information, registering online, requesting absentee ballots, joining the permanent absentee list, viewing sample ballots and finding County Clerk information.

deadlines.label: Registration Deadlines
deadlines.content: New Mexico's ordinary voter registration deadline is 28 days before an election. For the November 3, 2026 General Election, that date is October 6. Applications submitted by hand or mail may be accepted through the Friday following the registration deadline if they were completed or postmarked by the deadline. Eligible residents who miss ordinary registration may still use same-day registration during early voting and on Election Day at authorized locations.
deadlines.source_name: New Mexico Secretary of State — Voter Registration FAQ
deadlines.internal_note: The Secretary of State directly states that ordinary registration closes 28 days before an election under Section 1-4-8 NMSA 1978 and that same-day registration remains available. For November 3, 2026, 28 days before Election Day is October 6. Same-day registration is therefore important context and prevents the October 6 date from being presented as an absolute final opportunity to register.

polling_place.label: Find a Voting Location
polling_place.content: Use NMVOTE or the New Mexico Secretary of State's voting-location search to find voting locations. New Mexico counties may operate voter convenience centers where any registered voter in the county may cast a ballot, rather than requiring every voter to use a single traditional precinct polling place. Early-voting locations and Election Day locations can differ, so voters should check the official location information before voting.
polling_place.source_name: New Mexico Secretary of State — Voting Location Search
polling_place.internal_note: The Secretary of State homepage directly provides Search Voting Location Data and NMVOTE. New Mexico uses voter convenience centers in many jurisdictions, so avoid universally telling voters that they must report to one assigned precinct polling place. County Clerks publish authoritative local locations and hours.

election_day.label: Election Day Voting
election_day.content: New Mexico's General Election is Tuesday, November 3, 2026. Election Day voting locations are open from 7:00 a.m. until 7:00 p.m. A voter who is waiting in line when polls close may vote. New Mexico generally does not require an already-registered voter to present identification simply to cast a ballot. Identification requirements apply in certain situations, including same-day registration and certain first-time voters who registered by mail without previously providing the required identification.
election_day.source_name: New Mexico Secretary of State — Voting FAQ
election_day.internal_note: The Secretary of State confirms November 3, 2026 as the General Election. New Mexico Election Code establishes 7:00 a.m.-7:00 p.m. Election Day voting. New Mexico should not be characterized as a universal voter-ID state. Same-day registrants and certain first-time mail registrants have specific identification requirements.

polling_hours.label: Polling Hours
polling_hours.content: New Mexico Election Day polling locations are open from 7:00 a.m. until 7:00 p.m. A voter who is waiting in line at 7:00 p.m. is entitled to cast a ballot.
polling_hours.source_name: New Mexico Secretary of State — Voting FAQ
polling_hours.internal_note: New Mexico's statewide Election Day polling hours are 7:00 a.m.-7:00 p.m. The 7:00 p.m. close is also reflected in the Secretary of State's military and overseas guidance, which requires covered ballots to reach the County Clerk by close of polls.

early_voting.label: Early In-Person Voting
early_voting.content: New Mexico provides in-person early voting before Election Day. Voters may begin voting early at their County Clerk's office on the 28th day before the election. For the November 3, 2026 General Election, that date is October 6. Expanded early-voting locations are available in many counties beginning on the third Saturday before Election Day, which is October 17 in 2026. Early voting ends on Saturday, October 31. Locations, days and operating hours vary by county.
early_voting.source_name: New Mexico Secretary of State — Early Voting in Person
early_voting.internal_note: The Secretary of State directly states that County Clerk early voting begins 28 days before Election Day, expanded early voting is available in many counties beginning on the third Saturday before the election, and all early voting ends on the Saturday before Election Day. For November 3, 2026, these dates calculate to October 6, October 17 and October 31.

absentee_mail.label: Absentee Voting
absentee_mail.content: Any registered New Mexico voter may request an absentee ballot without providing an excuse. Voters may apply through NMVOTE or submit an absentee-ballot application to their County Clerk. Eligible voters may also join the permanent absentee list and automatically receive an absentee ballot for each statewide election. Completed absentee ballots must be received by the County Clerk no later than 7:00 p.m. on Election Day. Voters may return absentee ballots using authorized methods, including delivery to the County Clerk or a voting location in their county. Voters returning ballots by mail should send them early enough to ensure receipt by the deadline.
absentee_mail.glance_value: No excuse required; permanent absentee list available
absentee_mail.source_name: New Mexico Secretary of State — Absentee and Early Voting
absentee_mail.internal_note: The Secretary of State confirms no-excuse absentee voting, NMVOTE applications, ballot tracking, Election Day return options and the permanent absentee list. Ordinary absentee ballots must be received by 7:00 p.m. Election Day rather than merely postmarked by Election Day. New Mexico also provides an accessible electronic absentee-ballot delivery option for qualifying visually impaired voters, but the ballot is returned using the official return envelope.

voter_id.label: Voter ID Requirements
voter_id.content: New Mexico does not generally require an already-registered voter to show photo identification simply to vote in person. Certain first-time voters who registered by mail must provide identification if they did not provide the required identification with their registration application. Same-day registration has a separate identification requirement: the voter must present a physical identification document issued by a government, federally recognized Indian nation, tribe or pueblo, or educational institution that includes the voter's name and photograph. The document must also show the registration address or be accompanied by an accepted recent document showing the voter's name and matching address.
voter_id.glance_value: No general voter ID; ID required in specific cases
voter_id.source_name: New Mexico Secretary of State — Same Day Voter Registration FAQ
voter_id.internal_note: New Mexico should not be labeled a universal photo-ID state. The Secretary of State's provisional-voting guidance confirms the special rule for first-time mail registrants who failed to provide identification. Section 1-4-5.7 and the Secretary's same-day-registration guidance require physical photo identification plus matching address evidence when necessary for SDR. Expired identification can qualify because the SDR document need not have an expiration date and, if it does, the date need not be current.

accessible_voting.label: Accessible Voting
accessible_voting.content: New Mexico voters who are blind, physically disabled, unable to read or write, or members of a language minority may request assistance when voting. A voter may choose a person to provide assistance except the voter's employer, an agent of the employer, an officer or agent of the voter's union, or a candidate whose name appears on the ballot. New Mexico also provides an accessible absentee-ballot option that allows qualifying visually impaired voters to receive and independently mark an electronic ballot using screen-reader technology. The completed accessible absentee ballot must be returned using the procedures required by the state.
accessible_voting.glance_value: Voting assistance and accessible absentee ballots available
accessible_voting.source_name: New Mexico Secretary of State — Absentee and Early Voting
accessible_voting.internal_note: The Secretary of State's Voting FAQ directly establishes assistance rights under Sections 1-12-12 and 1-12-15 NMSA 1978. The absentee page confirms the electronic accessible absentee ballot for visually impaired voters using screen-reader technology. The official return envelope is mailed to the voter and must be used to return that ballot.

military_overseas.label: Military & Overseas Voting
military_overseas.content: New Mexico provides special voting procedures for eligible military members, qualifying family members and U.S. citizens living outside the United States. Covered voters may register using New Mexico's online system when eligible, the Federal Post Card Application or a New Mexico voter registration form. The Federal Post Card Application also serves as an absentee-ballot request. Eligible voters may receive their ballot by mail, email, secure web portal or fax and may return the ballot by mail, secure web portal, email or fax when the required waiver of ballot secrecy and affidavit are submitted. Military and overseas ballots must be received by the County Clerk by 7:00 p.m. on Election Day.
military_overseas.glance_value: FPCA and electronic ballot transmission and return available
military_overseas.source_name: New Mexico Secretary of State — Military and Overseas Voting
military_overseas.internal_note: The Secretary of State directly confirms FPCA registration and ballot requests, electronic delivery and electronic return methods, the secrecy-waiver requirement and the 7:00 p.m. Election Day receipt deadline. County Clerks can begin sending UOCAVA ballots 45 days before an election. New Mexico also allows an overseas citizen who never lived in New Mexico to qualify when the person's parent last resided in New Mexico, subject to the state's UOCAVA eligibility rules.

student_voting.label: College / Student Voting
student_voting.content: College students may register in New Mexico if they meet the state's voter eligibility and residency requirements. A student who establishes a qualifying New Mexico residence may use that address for voter registration. Students who maintain their voting residence elsewhere may continue voting under the rules applicable to that residence. New Mexico's registration procedures accept a student identification card as one of the documents that may be used in certain voter-registration and identification situations. A voter should maintain only one voting residence for an election.
student_voting.glance_value: Students may register at a qualifying New Mexico residence
student_voting.source_name: New Mexico Secretary of State — Voter Registration Information
student_voting.internal_note: New Mexico's current registration guidance expressly recognizes student identification cards among documents that can satisfy specified first-time registration identification requirements. The same-day-registration law also permits qualifying identification issued by an educational institution. The reader-facing language avoids claiming that college attendance alone establishes New Mexico residency.

sample_ballot.label: Official Sample Ballot
sample_ballot.content: New Mexico voters can use NMVOTE to view their sample ballot for an upcoming election. Because ballot contents depend on the voter's residential address and electoral districts, voters should use their own registration information to retrieve the sample ballot that applies to them. The 2026 General Election ballot should be checked again after all candidate and ballot-question certification is complete.
sample_ballot.glance_value: View your sample ballot through NMVOTE
sample_ballot.source_name: New Mexico Secretary of State — Voting & Elections
sample_ballot.internal_note: The Secretary of State's current Voting & Elections page directly identifies viewing the sample ballot for an upcoming election as an NMVOTE function. Because ballot content is voter-specific and may change during certification, reverify close to Election Day.

contact.label: Contact the State Election Authority
contact.content: New Mexico Secretary of State, Bureau of Elections, 325 Don Gaspar, Suite 300, Santa Fe, NM 87501. Elections phone: 505-827-3600. Toll-free: 1-800-477-3632. Email: Elections@sos.nm.gov. Regular office hours are Monday through Friday from 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. For voter-specific registration, absentee-ballot and voting-location questions, voters may also contact their County Clerk.
contact.source_name: New Mexico Secretary of State — Bureau of Elections
contact.internal_note: Current Secretary of State pages verify 505-827-3600, 1-800-477-3632, [Elections@sos.nm.gov](mailto:Elections@sos.nm.gov), the 325 Don Gaspar Suite 300 office and regular 8:00 a.m.-5:00 p.m. weekday hours. The email address is intentionally plain text with no Markdown or mailto wrapper.

official_resources.label: Official State & Local Resources
official_resources.content: Use the New Mexico Secretary of State Voting & Elections website and NMVOTE for official statewide voter information. NMVOTE provides voter registration, registration and election information, absentee-ballot requests, permanent absentee enrollment, sample ballots and County Clerk information. County Clerks administer voter registration, absentee voting, early voting and Election Day voting locations locally.
